name: RVDB 33-class viral classification by nearest-neighbour retrieval over frozen embeddings (Bůžková et al. 2026 Table 3)
description: Assign the organism label of the single nearest indexed training sequence to each test sequence, comparing pooling strategies across nine models.

attributes.protocol: Generate one frozen embedding per sequence by the stated pooling, L2-normalise, index the training embeddings with FAISS IndexFlatIP, retrieve the nearest neighbour (k = 1) for each test sequence and take its label. No parameter update.
attributes.aggregation: Share of the 4,950 test sequences labelled correctly
attributes.metric_implementation: Accuracy over test sequences; macro F1, precision and recall reported separately in Table 7
limitations: Nearest-neighbour probe over labelled reference embeddings, not zero-shot classification: the index holds the training labels (Section 2.7).
Point estimates from one fixed split with a fixed random seed; 95% Wilson intervals are quoted in the text, not in the tables.
RVDB organism labels are not a controlled taxonomy; the 33-class refinement removed seven ambiguous labels found through the models' own confusions (Sections 3.2 and 4).
ICTV reconciliation found one further redundant label pair still inside the 33-class dataset (Section 3.2; Section 4, Table 11).

name: RVDB viral classification: best frozen-embedding configuration against BLAST (Bůžková et al. 2026 Table 7)
description: Accuracy, macro F1, precision and recall for blastn, megablast and the best foundation-model configuration on the 40- and 33-class datasets.

attributes.protocol: Both pipelines index the same 350 training sequences per class. BLAST builds a nucleotide database from the training FASTA and takes the top hit's label (max_target_seqs = 1); the foundation model retrieves the nearest frozen embedding. Neither can return a label outside the reference set.
attributes.aggregation: Accuracy over test sequences; F1, precision and recall macro-averaged over classes
limitations: Nearest-neighbour probe over labelled reference embeddings, not zero-shot classification: the index holds the training labels (Section 2.7).
Point estimates from one fixed split with a fixed random seed; 95% Wilson intervals are quoted in the text, not in the tables.
RVDB organism labels are not a controlled taxonomy; the 33-class refinement removed seven ambiguous labels found through the models' own confusions (Sections 3.2 and 4).
Only the best foundation-model configuration (NTv3-650M, max pooling) appears in this table.
ICTV reconciliation found one further redundant label pair still inside the 33-class dataset (Section 3.2; Section 4, Table 11).

name: RVDB long-sequence viral classification, 16 classes (Bůžková et al. 2026 Table 10)
description: Classification of 84.6 to 409 kb viral genomes from about four indexed sequences per class, for four foundation models and blastn.

attributes.protocol: As for the primary dataset, but with about 4 indexed and about 16 queried sequences per class. NTv3-650M and blastn process each sequence whole; DNABERT-2, NTv2-50M and NTv2-250M are scored over overlapping chunks because their context window is shorter than these genomes.
attributes.aggregation: Pooled over test sequences; balanced accuracy, MCC and macro F1, precision and recall also reported
limitations: Nearest-neighbour probe over labelled reference embeddings, not zero-shot classification: the index holds the training labels (Section 2.7).
Point estimates from one fixed split with a fixed random seed; 95% Wilson intervals are quoted in the text, not in the tables.
RVDB organism labels are not a controlled taxonomy; the 33-class refinement removed seven ambiguous labels found through the models' own confusions (Sections 3.2 and 4).
Chunk-scored rows (DNABERT-2, NTv2-50M, NTv2-250M) are not computed on the same unit as the whole-sequence rows (Table 10 footnote a).
256 test sequences: the interval half-width near an accuracy of 0.95 is about 0.026, and the authors state the narrowing against BLAST is indicative only (Sections 2.9 and 3.8).
The long-sequence classes are more divergent viruses than the primary dataset's closely related subtypes, so dataset difficulty differs in more than sequence length (Section 4).
Pooling for the long-sequence run is not stated; the foundation-model rows use configurations with pooling unreported.
